claim: Nix's Linux build sandbox explicitly brings up the loopback interface inside the private network namespace: runChild() performs ioctl(SIOCSIFFLAGS) on 'lo' with flags IFF_UP | IFF_LOOPBACK | IFF_RUNNING, throwing 'cannot set loopback interface flags' on failure — so every sandboxed non-fixed-output build has a working 127.0.0.1.
stance_target: gap-04: the mosquitto-subprocess test harness (bind 127.0.0.1:0, spawn broker, TCP-probe) inside craneLib.cargoTest works as designed — no __noChroot or VM escape needed
scope_conditions: Nix 2.19.2 local-derivation-goal.cc; Linux; sandbox = true (default); non-fixed-output derivations
quoted_support: if (privateNetwork) { /* Initialise the loopback interface. */ ... strcpy(ifr.ifr_name, "lo"); ifr.ifr_flags = IFF_UP | IFF_LOOPBACK | IFF_RUNNING; if (ioctl(fd.get(), SIOCSIFFLAGS, &ifr) == -1) throw SysError("cannot set loopback interface flags"); }

claim: The sandbox child is cloned with CLONE_NEWPID | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWIPC | CLONE_NEWUTS | CLONE_PARENT | SIGCHLD, plus CLONE_NEWNET only for non-fixed-output derivations ('Fixed-output derivations are not run in a private network namespace to allow functions like fetchurl to work'), so craneLib.cargoTest builds (normal derivations) always get the private netns with the UP lo interface.
stance_target: gap-04: cargoTest/cargo build derivations are ordinary sandboxed builds, hence netns + loopback apply
quoted_support: options.cloneFlags = CLONE_NEWPID | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWIPC | CLONE_NEWUTS | CLONE_PARENT | SIGCHLD; if (privateNetwork) options.cloneFlags |= CLONE_NEWNET;

claim: Nix's own sandbox design comment states the private network namespace 'only has a private loopback interface' and that the fixed-output exception exists solely to let fetchers reach the network — the in-sandbox loopback is the intended (and only) networking surface for build-time tests.
stance_target: gap-04: design intent — in-sandbox loopback TCP is a supported, intended use, not an implementation accident
quoted_support: The private network namespace ensures that the builder cannot talk to the outside world (or vice versa). It only has a private loopback interface. (Fixed-output derivations are not run in a private network namespace to allow functions like fetchurl to work.)
